title: KV prefix policy orchestration and safety gates for cost-aware caching
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Deliver an automated recommendation and safe-apply system that proposes KV/prefix cache key designs and TTL policies tailored to customer workloads, simulates expected hit-rate and cost savings, and executes staged rollouts with strong rollback guarantees. This ticket covers the modeling, a traffic synthesizer for edge cases, the validation harness, new safety gates for live config apply, and an initial Console integration for visibility and approvals.

Scope: offline hit-rate estimator, workload synth tool, conservative TTL suggester, staged apply orchestration (dry-run -> canary -> phased), runtime invariants for safe rollback, and a follow-up post-apply verification job that monitors divergence from predictions. Not in scope: full auto-apply without manual approval, cross-customer policy sharing, or UI polish beyond initial Console panels.

Why: Current manual TTL/key tuning is a major source of unit-cost waste. Teams often over- or under-cache due to incomplete visibility. A reproducible simulation + safe apply flow will reduce token cost and operator time while limiting risk to latency and correctness.
acceptance_criteria: A1: A synthetic workload generator that can replay sampled prefixes and produce tail-heavy patterns for validation (repro scripts + dataset) exists in repo and has docs.
A2: Offline hit-rate estimator produces TTL suggestions and expected hit-rate / cost delta per prefix; results validated against historical holdout for >=95% confidence on median workloads.
A3: Orchestration workflow supports dry-run, canary (1% traffic), phased ramp (1% -> 10% -> 50%), and an automated rollback trigger based on deviation thresholds.
A4: Console shows suggestion details, predicted savings, risk score, and exposes an approval button that kicks off the staged apply.
A5: Post-apply validator runs for 24h and verifies observed hit-rate vs predicted; it generates an auto-rollback if thresholds exceeded and posts a report to #runtime-alerts and the ticket.
A6: End-to-end tests added: simulator vs live sampling matching within tolerance on a selected customer testbed; CI gate for the orchestration code.
A7: Security review flag set and basic KMS access checks included for config write operations.
A8: Runbook added for SRE on how to inspect and manually revert applied policies and how to interpret the safety metrics.
comments: 2025-02-24 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff. Drafted acceptance criteria and scope. Identified two primary risks: underestimation of prefix variance and risk of cascading rollbacks during noisy traffic windows. Linked to a quick spike runbook.

2025-02-26 - Connor Lee: Implemented initial traffic sampler and baseline holdout test. Early results show high variance in 0.1% of prefixes; plan to treat those as 'volatile' and exclude from aggressive TTLs.
2025-02-28 - Ingrid Müller (Product): Reviewed prediction UX. Requested explicit risk score and a small explanation of model inputs in the Console panel. Added as acceptance item.

2025-03-01 - Connor Lee: Submitted draft PR gh: redwood/runtime#1287 with simulator and estimator. Running infra CI; unit tests for the estimator included. Marked PR as WIP; awaiting integration tests.

2025-03-03 - SRE - Rahul Banerjee: Reviewed canary orchestration. Suggested adding time-of-day blackout windows to avoid rollouts during known high-variance maintenance windows. Added as a safety gate.
2025-03-04 - Connor Lee: Updated orchestration to support blackout windows and added an emergency manual stop API. Updated ticket with rollout plan and metrics to monitor.
2025-03-04 - Aisha Patel: Scheduled demo for cross-functional review on 2025-03-07. Asked PM and Design to validate Console mocks prior to demo.
decision: Implement conservative default TTLs with explicit volatility tagging. Use a two-stage estimator: (1) historical holdout estimator for median traffic and (2) worst-case synthesizer to surface volatile prefixes. Only prefixes with stable predictions and positive ROI will be eligible for phased apply. Blackout windows and an emergency stop API are required before any canary runs.
